45822: The International Congress on World Evangelization, led by Billy Graham and with John Stott as chief drafter of the Covenant, affirms that evangelism and socio-political involvement are both part of Christian duty, while stating that in the church's mission of sacrificial service evangelism is primary.
45824: Andy Crouch argues that the only way to change culture is to make more and better culture, and that Christians should move beyond condemning, critiquing, copying or consuming culture toward cultivating and creating it.
45826: In *What Is the Mission of the Church?* Kevin DeYoung and Greg Gilbert argue that the church's distinct mission is to make disciples through proclaiming the gospel, while affirming that Christians should do good works and that ordinary vocations honour God. Their book is a careful counterweight to calls for 'holistic' mission.
45828: Tim Keller, with Katherine Leary Alsdorf, presents work as part of God's good design, damaged by sin and redeemed through the gospel. The book draws on Luther and Sayers and helped spread the 'faith and work' movement. (Two years earlier, the Lausanne Cape Town Commitment of 2010 named the sacred-secular divide as a major obstacle to mission.)
45830: Painter Makoto Fujimura calls Christians to 'culture care': tending culture like a garden, offering beauty as a gift rather than a weapon in culture wars. He develops this in *Art and Faith: A Theology of Making* (2020).
45831: Gifts and talents: what they are, and how each can be expression and witness
45832: Filter by colour. Each card names a gift, shows where Scripture mentions it, gives people who show it, and describes how it can be both an expression of love and worship and a witness to Christ. The spiritual-gift lists are already in the Gifts section of the app; here the focus is on how each gift is used.
45833: Speaking a word from God that strengthens, encourages and comforts (1 Cor 14:3).
45834: Christians disagree on whether prophecy today means new revelation, Spirit-prompted insight, or faithful preaching. Expression: it is love speaking truth to build others up. Witness: Paul says an outsider who hears prophecy may be convicted and declare that God is truly among you (1 Cor 14:24-25).
45835: Explaining God's word clearly so others understand and obey.
45836: Teachers carry extra responsibility (Jas 3:1). Expression: delight in truth and in other people's growth. Witness: clear teaching equips the whole church for its work in the world (Eph 4:12).
45837: Coming alongside people to urge, comfort and strengthen them.
45838: Barnabas' name means 'son of encouragement' (Acts 4:36). Expression: compassion in words. Witness: Barnabas vouched for Paul and saw grace in Antioch, and 'a great many people were added to the Lord' (Acts 11:23-24).
45842: Paul asks givers to give with generosity or simplicity (Rom 12:8) and cheerfully (2 Cor 9:7). Expression: joy in God's generosity. Witness: the Gentile collection for Jerusalem showed one family across ethnic lines, and those who received it would glorify God (2 Cor 9:12-13).
45846: Guiding a community with care and diligence; the Greek word in 1 Cor 12:28 pictures a ship's pilot.
45847: Expression: ordering a community so that others can flourish. Witness: when the apostles organised fair food distribution, 'the word of God continued to increase' (Acts 6:1-7).
45850: Caring for the suffering, sick and poor, done 'with cheerfulness' (Rom 12:8).
45851: Expression: it mirrors the mercy of God. Witness: early Christian care for the sick in plagues impressed even critics. Mercy should not be withheld from those who will never believe (Luke 6:35-36).
45854: Practical, often unseen work that keeps the body functioning.
45855: 'Helps' in 1 Cor 12:28 appears only there. Expression: humble love like Jesus washing feet (John 13:14-15). Witness: Peter says those who serve should do so in God's strength 'so that in everything God may be glorified' (1 Pet 4:11).
45857: Welcoming strangers and believers into one's home and table.
45858: Peter links hospitality directly to using gifts (1 Pet 4:9-10). Expression: the warmth of God's welcome. Witness: Lydia's house became the base of the church in Philippi (Acts 16:14-15, Acts 16:40).
45862: Spirit-given insight for a situation or understanding of God's ways.
45863: Interpreters differ on whether these are revelatory or wise teaching. Expression: helping people see clearly. Witness: Jesus promised the Spirit would give words to believers on trial before rulers (Luke 21:14-15).
45865: Unusual trust in God for a particular task or need.
45866: Different from the saving faith every believer has. Expression: it encourages a whole community to trust God. Witness: answered prayer and courage in hardship make people ask where the hope comes from.
45868: God's power to heal and do signs through believers.
45869: Continuationists and cessationists disagree about whether these continue (see /debates/cessationism). Expression: compassion; Jesus healed because he was moved with pity (Mark 1:41). Witness: signs drew attention to the message in Acts (Acts 3:6-16), but Jesus also healed many who did not follow him.
45871: Telling the difference between what comes from God and what does not.
45872: Expression: protecting people out of love. Witness: a church that is not easily deceived is a safer place for seekers (1 John 4:1).
45876: Speaking in languages not learned, with interpretation for the church.
45877: Paul values tongues for private prayer but asks for interpretation in church so that others are built up (1 Cor 14:2-5). Expression: prayer beyond words. Witness: at Pentecost hearers heard God's works in their own languages (Acts 2:5-11), but Paul warns that uninterpreted tongues may confuse outsiders (1 Cor 14:23).
45880: A particular gift for announcing the gospel and leading people to faith.
45881: Not every believer has this gift (Eph 4:11), though all can witness. Expression: joy in good news and love for people. Witness: this is its direct purpose, and the church should honour and support those who have it.
45883: Sent to start and establish churches where Christ is not known.
45884: Whether 'apostle' continues as a role is debated; many use it loosely for pioneer mission. Expression: obedience and love for the unreached. Witness: Paul's ambition was to preach where Christ had not been named (Rom 15:20).
45886: Caring for a flock: feeding, guarding and seeking the lost.
45887: Expression: the care of the Good Shepherd (John 10:11). Witness: shepherds are to be examples to the flock (1 Pet 5:2-3) and well thought of by outsiders (1 Tim 3:7).
45890: Skill in metal, wood, stone and design, given by the Spirit.
45891: Bezalel is the first person 'filled with the Spirit of God' (Exod 31:3). Expression: making beautiful, durable things in the image of the Maker. Witness: Solomon's temple, made with the skill of Hiram of Tyre, drew the nations' attention to Israel's God (1 Kgs 8:41-43).
45894: Skilled women spun and wove for the tabernacle; Dorcas sewed for widows.
45895: Exodus calls the women who spun 'wise-hearted' (Exod 35:25-26). Expression: care made visible in cloth. Witness: Dorcas' garments were shown with tears when she died, and after she was raised 'many believed in the Lord' (Acts 9:39-42).
45899: Playing and singing with skill, for God and for people.
45900: David's playing brought relief to Saul (1 Sam 16:23), and trained musicians led temple worship (1 Chr 25:7). Expression: lament, joy and praise. Witness: Paul and Silas singing in prison were heard by the other prisoners (Acts 16:25), and the Psalms call the nations to sing (Ps 96:1-3).
45904: Shaping language with beauty and depth.
45905: About a third of the Old Testament is poetry. Expression: Ps 45:1 pictures a heart overflowing with a good theme and a tongue like the pen of a ready writer. Witness: poems and hymns teach and carry the faith across generations (Col 3:16).
45908: Colour, form and pattern for glory and beauty.
45909: The priests' garments were to be made 'for glory and for beauty' (Exod 28:2) with pomegranates and gold bells. Expression: beauty that needs no extra justification. Witness: beauty can awaken longing for God that argument alone does not reach.
45913: Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem's walls in 52 days. Expression: securing a city's welfare. Witness: the nations around 'perceived that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God' (Neh 6:15-16).
45915: Working and keeping the earth to feed others.
45916: Isaiah says God himself instructs the farmer in when to plough and how to thresh (Isa 28:23-29). Expression: obedience to the first command to work and keep the garden. Witness: Ruth and Boaz's harvest field becomes a place of kindness and covenant loyalty (Ruth 2:8-12).
45917: Uzziah, who loved the soil (2 Chr 26:10)
45919: Running organisations and nations wisely and honestly.
45920: Joseph managed Egypt's grain; Daniel served foreign kings so faithfully that his enemies could find no fault (Dan 6:4). Expression: justice and order for the common good. Witness: Pharaoh recognised the Spirit of God in Joseph (Gen 41:38), and Darius praised Daniel's God (Dan 6:25-27).
45922: Producing and selling goods honestly to meet needs.
45923: Lydia sold purple cloth; the capable woman of Proverbs 31 buys a field and sells garments. Expression: creativity, provision and generosity (Prov 31:20). Witness: Lydia's business network and home became the first church in Europe (Acts 16:14-15).
45925: Working with one's hands to avoid being a burden.
45926: Paul worked as a tentmaker or leatherworker (Acts 18:3). Expression: dignity of ordinary labour and love that refuses to burden others. Witness: Paul presented his work as an example of the gospel's freely given grace (1 Thess 2:9, Acts 20:34-35).
45928: Studying God's world and human wisdom.
45929: Solomon spoke of trees, animals, birds and fish (1 Kgs 4:33); Daniel and his friends were given skill in all learning (Dan 1:17). Expression: delight in God's works (Ps 111:2). Witness: kings came to hear Solomon's wisdom (1 Kgs 4:34).
45931: Medicine and care of the body
45933: Paul calls Luke 'the beloved physician' (Col 4:14). Expression: honouring the body God made. Witness: Christian hospitals and medical missions have carried both compassion and the gospel, at best without making care conditional on belief.
45936: Luke 'carefully investigated everything' to write an orderly account (Luke 1:1-4). Expression: love of truth. Witness: his purpose was that Theophilus might know the certainty of what he had been taught.
45940: Eloquence and the ability to reason in public.
45941: Apollos was eloquent and competent in the Scriptures, and he 'powerfully refuted' opponents in public (Acts 18:24-28). Expression: love for clear truth. Witness: direct. Paul also warns against trusting eloquence rather than the cross (1 Cor 2:1-5).
45944: Joy expressed with the whole body.
45945: Miriam led women with tambourines and dancing after the sea crossing (Exod 15:20-21); David danced before the LORD with all his might (2 Sam 6:14). Expression: whole-body praise. Witness: public celebration showed what God had done, though Michal despised it (2 Sam 6:16).
45947: Raising and teaching children in daily life.
45948: Israel was to teach God's words at home, on the road, lying down and rising (Deut 6:6-7). Expression: love that shapes a life. Witness: Timothy's faith came first through his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice (2 Tim 1:5).
45950: Bringing understanding and order to the created world.
45951: Adam's first task after work in the garden is to name the animals (Gen 2:19-20). Expression: sharing God's ordering of chaos in Genesis 1. Witness: when humans rule as caring stewards, creation itself shows the character of its King (Ps 8:3-9).
45957: To bring people to faith in Christ; a gift is valuable as a means to evangelism.
45958: To reflect God's image, love neighbours and honour God; a gift is good in itself.
45959: Both: gifts glorify God and serve people in themselves, and that faithful work also witnesses and opens doors for the gospel.
45961: Conversations started, decisions made, people reached.
45962: Faithfulness, skill, beauty, truth and real benefit to others.
45963: Faithfulness and love first; fruitfulness in witness is hoped for but left to God (1 Cor 3:6-7).
45965: A concert with an altar call; a café run mainly to reach customers; a novel written to carry a gospel message.
45966: A Christian composer writing an honest symphony; a nurse caring well without mentioning faith.
45967: A well-run business with fair wages whose owner prays for customers and speaks of Christ when trust allows.
45973: Takes eternity seriously; keeps the church from forgetting to speak; channels great energy into mission.
45974: Honours creation and craft; frees believers from guilt; treats people as neighbours, not targets.
45975: Holds together creation and redemption, word and deed; fits the whole Bible's story.
45977: Sacred/secular split; art as propaganda; people as projects; burnout and guilt; weak craft.
45978: Silence about Christ; witness becomes vague; comfort with the world as it is; neglect of the lost.
45979: Can become vague 'both/and' that never prioritises; each side may suspect it dilutes their concern.
45980: Many revivalists and mass evangelists; some mission agencies; popular youth and church culture.
45981: Many artists and craftspeople; Catholic and Orthodox traditions of beauty; some Kuyperian voices; Jewish teaching on avodah.
45982: Lausanne movement, John Stott, Tim Keller, Andy Crouch, Makoto Fujimura, Dorothy Sayers, Francis Schaeffer.
45984: These are real positions held by sincere Christians. Most do not deny the other pole entirely; they differ on emphasis and priority. Place yourself, then read the position on the other side as its best defenders would put it.
45986: Mainly expression of the image of God and love of neighbour
45988: The world is a sinking ship and time is short. Every gift, from singing to business, should be harnessed to rescue souls. This view grew from real love and urgency and fuelled great missionary sacrifice.
45989: Many nineteenth- and twentieth-century revivalists (Finney, Moody); parts of mass-evangelism culture
45991: Christians should do good works and honour God in their jobs, but the church's unique mission is making disciples. Because eternal destinies are at stake, proclamation has priority, and this should shape how gifts are directed.
45992: Kevin DeYoung and Greg Gilbert; John Piper (with his stress that worship, not missions, is the ultimate goal); many Great-Commission-focused evangelicals
45994: Evangelism and social responsibility are both Christian duty and belong together, like two wings, but in the church's mission evangelism is primary. Gifts serve both word and deed.
45995: Lausanne Covenant (1974); John Stott; the Grand Rapids report (1982)
45997: Word and deed are inseparable parts of one mission. Ordinary work is a calling, and the sacred/secular divide must go. Witness flows from integrated lives rather than from added messages.
45998: Latin American theologians René Padilla and Samuel Escobar; Tim Keller; Andy Crouch; the Cape Town Commitment (2010)
46000: Gifts are first for building a visible community that lives the way of Jesus: sharing, peacemaking, simple living. The church's life together is its witness, more than individual achievement or cultural influence.
46001: Mennonite and Anabaptist traditions; John Howard Yoder; Stanley Hauerwas (influenced by this tradition)
46003: Christ claims every square inch of life. Science, art, politics and business are callings in their own right, with their own God-given standards, not merely platforms for evangelism.
46004: Abraham Kuyper; Herman Bavinck; Hans Rookmaaker; Al Wolters; Richard Mouw; Francis Schaeffer (in his writing on art)
46006: Beauty, liturgy, icons and craft can make God's presence and goodness visible. Art serves worship and the human person; it is not reducible to a message.
46007: Catholic tradition (John Paul II, *Letter to Artists*, 1999); Orthodox iconography and liturgy; Anglican and high-church traditions
46009: The artist offers beauty gratuitously, as God made the world, and tends culture like a garden. Making art only to win arguments damages both the art and the gospel.
46010: Makoto Fujimura; Dorothy L. Sayers; J. R. R. Tolkien's idea of 'sub-creation'; many Christian artists
46012: What does it mean that the first person 'filled with the Spirit' is a craftsman?
46014: God calls Bezalel 'by name' and fills him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all craftsmanship (Exod 31:2-3). The language matches the way the Spirit equips prophets and kings.
46016: The tabernacle, its furniture, the priests' garments 'for glory and for beauty' (Exod 28:2). Their work is for worship, but much of it is ornament: almond blossoms, pomegranates, cherubim. Beauty is part of the purpose.
46018: God also gives them the ability to teach others (Exod 35:34). Gifts are passed on in community, and many 'wise-hearted' men and women join the work (Exod 36:1-2).
46020: Straight after the call comes the Sabbath command (Exod 31:12-17). Later Jewish teaching derived the categories of work forbidden on the Sabbath from the labours of building the tabernacle (Talmud, Shabbat 49b). Holy work is good, and it still stops for rest.
46021: Artistic skill can be a direct gift of the Spirit, given for worship and beauty, taught in community and bounded by rest. It did not need to 'lead to evangelism' to be holy.
46023: Is it ministry when a gifted person simply helps someone who suffers?
46025: Saul is tormented by a harmful spirit, and his servants look for 'a man who is skilful in playing the lyre' (1 Sam 16:16).
46027: He is skilful in playing, a man of valour, prudent in speech, of good presence, 'and the LORD is with him' (1 Sam 16:18). Skill and godliness are named together.
46029: When David plays, Saul is refreshed and the harmful spirit departs (1 Sam 16:23). There is no sermon; the music itself is the service.
46031: The same gift later produces psalms that Israel sang for centuries. David's music served one troubled king and also became a witness to the nations (Ps 57:9).
46032: A skill used with care for one suffering person is real service to God. Over time, such faithfulness can become a far wider witness than anyone planned.
46034: How does practical craft become both love and witness?
46036: Luke calls Tabitha (Dorcas) a disciple 'full of good works and acts of charity' (Acts 9:36). Her name is given in both Aramaic and Greek, which may suggest she moved in both communities.
46038: At her death the widows weep and show Peter the tunics and garments she made while she was with them (Acts 9:39). Her love was stitched into clothing for the poor.
46040: Peter prays and she is raised, and it 'became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord' (Acts 9:42). Strictly, the miracle led to faith; but it was her life of love that drew the grieving community together.
46042: The text does not say she sewed in order to evangelise. It presents her work as good in itself, and God used it within a larger witness.
46043: Ordinary craft offered in love is honoured by God and remembered by the church; witness grew around a life of mercy rather than replacing it.
46045: Was Paul's trade only a way to fund 'real' ministry?
46047: Paul stays with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth 'because he was of the same trade', working as tentmakers (Acts 18:3). The Greek word may mean leatherworker; scholars debate the details.
46049: He worked night and day so as not to burden anyone while preaching (1 Thess 2:9), and to give an example of honest work to idle believers (2 Thess 3:7-9). He also gave up his right to support so the gospel would be free of charge (1 Cor 9:12-18).
46050: The workshop as a place of witness
46051: Ancient workshops were places of conversation. Many scholars (for example Ronald Hock) suggest Paul's workshop was itself a setting for teaching.
46053: Paul did value his work partly for the gospel's sake. Yet he also told ordinary believers to work quietly with their hands to win the respect of outsiders and depend on no one (1 Thess 4:11-12), and to work so they could share with those in need (Eph 4:28).
46054: Paul shows the integrated view: honest manual work has dignity, supports others and also serves the gospel. Both instrument and expression are present, and neither cancels the other.
46056: What does Jesus say about an extravagant gift with no practical use?
46058: A woman breaks a jar of costly nard, worth about a year's wages, and pours it on Jesus' head (Mark 14:3-5).
46060: Some say it should have been sold and given to the poor. Their logic is efficiency: a gift is valued by its usefulness.
46062: 'She has done a beautiful thing to me' (Mark 14:6). The Greek kalon ergon means a good or beautiful work. Jesus defends an act of pure devotion and links it to his coming burial (Mark 14:8).
46064: Jesus says that wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will be told in memory of her (Mark 14:9). An act with no evangelistic purpose became part of the gospel's own proclamation.
46065: Worship and beauty offered to Jesus need no further justification, and God may weave such expression into the gospel's witness far beyond our planning.
46067: How does faithful work in a non-Christian setting honour God?
46069: Daniel serves Babylonian and Persian kings as an exile. Jeremiah had told exiles to seek the welfare of the city and pray for it (Jer 29:7).
46071: He distinguishes himself because 'an excellent spirit was in him', and the king plans to set him over the whole kingdom (Dan 6:3). His rivals can find no corruption or negligence (Dan 6:4).
46073: The only charge they can bring concerns his God. He keeps praying three times a day toward Jerusalem (Dan 6:10).
46074: After the lions' den, Darius writes to all peoples that they should fear the God of Daniel (Dan 6:25-27). Daniel's witness rested on years of competent, honest work and visible devotion.
46075: Competent, honest service in a secular workplace is itself faithfulness to God, and combined with open devotion it can become a public witness.
